title: Rate Limiting Implementation
summary: We apply rate limiting with standard response headers and choose algorithms like token bucket based on burst-handling requirements to protect the API and ensure fair usage.

content.overview: We enforce rate limiting on our APIs to guard against abuse and guarantee equitable access. The implementation exposes standard headers and selects an algorithm that fits burst tolerance needs.
content.details: We evaluate token bucket, fixed window, and sliding window log algorithms. Token bucket is preferred when we need to allow bursts while maintaining an average rate; fixed window is simpler but can suffer from boundary double-spend issues. Whichever algorithm is used, our responses always include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset headers so clients can adapt their request pacing.
content.examples: Response header example: X-RateLimit-Limit: 100, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 45, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1620000000.
content.caveats: Fixed window counters are susceptible to boundary problems where clients send requests at the edge of two windows; choose token bucket or sliding logs when this is unacceptable.
